cases.title: Find and edit a setting
cases.match: Matched: AUDIO, USB AUDIO, FOLLOWS KNOB, pattern1, tempo125 and stopped transport. Part909 follows the actual boot header and unchanged inputs. Hidden project/storage state is not verified identical.
cases.stayed: Category groups, selection highlight, K2 movement, K3 editing, arrow/back rules and control hints already exist.
cases.changed: The selected name and value use a two-line16/18px card on a fixed left edge. Context rows use a24px grid; two13px help lines replace the crowded footer treatment.
cases.cost: Only four rows are visible. The baseline PERFORM tiles are not reproduced; their quick-control visibility is an unresolved integration tradeoff. No control behaviour is implemented here.
steps: GLOBE opens Settings; K2 selects AUDIO; > enters.
K2 selects USB AUDIO; K3 edits. < or PATCH backs.
Full PATCH/GLOBE exit resets focus on next entry.

cases.title: Request SAVE and read the boundary
cases.match: Same PROJECT/SAVE target, pattern1/tempo125 and running transport. Outcome coverage differs deliberately: the actual before is queued feedback; the proposal only acknowledges an input.
cases.stayed: Actual25.1 already acknowledges SAVE with SAVES WHEN STOPPED. This is existing functionality, not a new proposal feature.
cases.changed: The model now visibly counts each received SAVE/LOAD input instead of changing only an off-screen counter. It makes no acceptance, save-success or loaded-data claim.
cases.cost: Queued/result/error lifecycle is not integrated. Preset and held-note policy still owns that source-bound layer. Read-only REF samples and actual baseline evidence are references, not produced outcomes; this remains a dependency.
steps: SCALE requests; K3 and arrows never run the action.
A real result must come from the existing authoritative lifecycle. STOP/time alone is not SAVED.

cases.title: Cancel a question without surprises
cases.match: Matched: RESET PROJECT question, SAMPLES ARE KEPT, pattern1/tempo125 and stopped transport. No reset is confirmed in baseline capture.
cases.stayed: The question, explicit SCALE confirmation, PATCH cancellation and restored row already exist.
cases.changed: Question text and controls align to the same12px left inset. Native help now names SEQ PLAY cancellation plus its start/stop effect; GLOBE remains ignored.
cases.cost: This preserves the source policy: PLAY can interrupt a running pattern. Clip transport is a different intercepted route. The proposal does not make PLAY a harmless universal Back.
steps: SCALE opens the selected destructive question.
PATCH cancels and restores the exact row.
Normal SEQ PLAY cancels plus starts/stops; clip mode is delegated.

cases.title: Read peer identity and leave clearly
cases.match: Matched: BLUETOOTH / NAME with no displayed peer name, pattern1/tempo125 and stopped transport. No real Bluetooth connection is claimed.
cases.stayed: NAME is already read only; the baseline has a bounded name row and generic back/help.
cases.changed: Focus expands names in the body, preserving escape help. Zero/one/two, maximum20-character names and disconnect snapshots are inspectable in the walkthrough.
cases.cost: Connected-peer before frames were not available. The two-name and marquee replacement are proposed fixture evidence only; actual pairing and hardware readability remain untested.
steps: Read both names without losing back/exit guidance.
Try empty, one20-character, two20-character and changed snapshots using inspection fixtures.

cases.title: Read battery without overstating power
cases.match: Matched: SYSTEM / BATTERY FULL, pattern1/tempo125 and stopped transport. FULL is actual emulator LCD output, not a physical battery measurement.
cases.stayed: The BATTERY row and FULL/USB POWER/unknown semantics already exist and remain read only.
cases.changed: The selected readout is larger and visually separate from action rows. Display-only samples retain all source labels, including unknown (...).
cases.cost: Ordinary-playing power visibility belongs to the whole-firmware integration owner. No competing persistent header, charging state or physical Elite/Pro result is proposed here.
steps: K3 and arrows cannot edit the reading.
USB POWER and unknown samples are labelled inspection inputs.

cases.title: See the local-key boundary while playing
cases.match: Partial match: Global first category, tempo125, running transport and held physical F4 gesture. Before is supplied actual25.1 input/LCD evidence; after is the94197fc8 source-rule model. Persistence state and audio are not matched.
cases.stayed: Global entry and source-local-key ownership restrictions are existing behaviours. RUN describes pattern transport; it does not prove a held voice survives.
cases.changed: The native KEY RETIRED badge exposes the ownership boundary inside Settings. It remains visible during later input acknowledgement.
cases.cost: No audible continuity or tail measurement was made. This is truthful loss communication, not a sustained-note continuity fix. Source versions differ and physical behaviour remains unqualified.
steps: Hold local F4 in the Chicago part-B fixture, then enter Global.
Observe KEY RETIRED separately from RUN.
Use back/exit without interpreting RUN as proof of sustained sound.
